big: Rohan paid ₹1 lakh tax in India on a gain. His country of residence also wants tax on the same gain. Without help he pays twice. With a treaty and the right papers, he claims credit and pays the higher of the two, not both.

lines: Is there a way to stop being taxed twice?
Yes. A DTAA between the two countries decides who taxes what. A tax residency certificate and a foreign tax credit help you claim it. When both countries say you are resident, a tie-breaker decides.

rows: A treaty deciding who may tax which income, and at what rate
Proof you live in your country for tax

Decides which country treats you as resident
